title: Noise robust self testing from genuine local operation shared randomness multipartite nonlocality Tests
abstract: Violation of the $N$-partite inequality introduced in Phys. Rev. Lett. 129, 150401 (2022) for genuine multipartite nonlocality under local operations and shared randomness (LOSR) rules out all causal-network models obtained by locally composing arbitrary resources involving at most $N-1$ parties, even when supplemented by shared randomness among all $N$ parties. Here, we demonstrate a device-independent self-test protocol for this. We further establish an analytic noise-robust self-test. For a Bell-score deficit $ε$, we derive explicit $O(\sqrtε)$ vector-norm bounds for the state and the corresponding measurement actions.
summary: This paper provides a comprehensive theoretical framework for self-testing genuine multipartite nonlocality under local operations and shared randomness. It derives an explicit, noise-robust bound showing how the measured deviation from the theoretical maximum violation constrains the fidelity of the unknown quantum state. This advances the understanding of device-independent certification of quantum resources.
main_problem: The paper develops a device-independent, noise-robust self-testing protocol for genuine multipartite nonlocality under Local Operations and Shared Randomness (LOSR).
main_result: It establishes an explicit analytic bound on the fidelity ($F_N$) of the state, showing that the nonlocality deficit ($\epsilon$) directly constrains the deviation from the ideal quantum state.
method: The core methodology involves using Sum-of-Squares (SOS) decomposition to relate the nonlocality functional deficit to sums of squared norms of residual operators, which are then bounded to determine robustness.
model_or_system: The study concerns N-partite quantum systems ($N \ge 3$) and the violation of an N-partite inequality that rules out causal models based on local operations and shared randomness.
key_observables: The nonlocality functional $S_N$, the quantum maximum $ eta_Q^N$, and the deficit $\epsilon =  eta_Q^N - \langle S_N angle$.
important_parameters: The number of parties $N$, the noise deficit $\epsilon$, and the fidelity $F_N$.
main_assumptions: The derivation assumes the existence of a strategy achieving the maximum quantum violation and relies on techniques like Naimark dilation and SOS decomposition.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the nonlocality functional and establishing the self-testing framework via SOS decomposition, to deriving operator identities, constructing local isometries, and finally extending the result to provide an analytic noise-robust bound on the fidelity.
why_interesting: The rigorous connection between experimentally measurable nonlocality violations and the underlying quantum state structure is fundamental to quantum foundations and device-independent quantum information tasks.
